answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III, deal 5 of 9 Conflict II on top, then 1 of 3 Conflict I on top, making 10 (I×1, II×5, III×4). Return unused cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Four-player: score 1; three-player: score 0. Both start with 2 Agents on Leader, a third Swordmaster Agent beside board, 3 troops in garrison and 9 in supply (12 total), and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: “on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space”; “Place two Agents on your Leader”; “three [troops] ... remaining nine”; “Take 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal with Agents left; after Revealing you skip turns for the rest of the phase and cannot later Agent. Reveal effects come from cards remaining in hand. Agent-turn and revealed cards are cleaned up together into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents”; Reveal: remaining hand and Clean Up all cards to discard.

answers.answer: Only resources gained from a Plot Intrigue before Agent placement may pay entry. Effects from the played Agent card or destination occur after entry and cannot. One card sends only one Agent, using one icon; a card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot gains before entry can pay; Agent Turn: one Agent icon; “A card with no Agent icons can’t be played on an Agent turn.”

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from garrison: 5 total in this example. At a non-Combat space you cannot deploy. Recruits come from personal supply into garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: “any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more ... from your garrison”; recruit from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: Spy Agent icon sends an Agent to a board space connected to your Spy without recalling it; you still need that card icon. Infiltrate recalls a connected Spy to enter an opponent-occupied space. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing your Agent but before any effects, to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent icon; Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence timing; “cannot recall the same Spy to both.”

answers.answer: Strength is 11: 2 troops ×2 = 4, one sandworm = 3, and four swords = 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you are ineligible for Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop=2, worm=3, sword=1; last unit removed means 0. Combat: only players with at least one unit may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes. A player may act again after an earlier pass; the window closes after all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to supply (not garrison), Combat markers reset to 0, and sandworms return to bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; “pass consecutively”; Combat cleanup passage.

answers.answer: Four players tied for first each take the second reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. In a three-player game, same result and no other rewards. A zero-strength player gets no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first each gain second reward; nobody wins/takes card; zero strength receives none.

answers.answer: One or more worms double rewards once; two worms do not quadruple. Control and battle-icon rewards cannot be doubled. Optional paid reward can be repeated by paying again: 3 spice for 1 VP becomes 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “one or more”; control and battle icons cannot; may pay a cost a second time.

answers.answer: Check after winning and taking the Conflict card: match any face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply with same icon, then must flip the pair face down for 1 VP. Endgame wild matches any of the three icons.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: “When you win a Conflict”; face-up Conflict or Objective; must flip; wild icon during Endgame.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP, lost below 2 and regained on returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, retained after dropping below 4 and re-earned on returning; first to 4 also gets Alliance +1 VP. Tying the holder does not take Alliance; an opponent must rise higher.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: 2 VP reversal; 4 track bonus retained; Alliance transfer requires rising higher.

answers.answer: Persuasion is spent during Reveal, before, between, or after Reveal effects. It may be pooled for a card or split among cards. The Row refills immediately, so its replacement may also be bought. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: during Reveal, pool/split, Row always five; acquired card into discard.

answers.answer: Each empty Maker space gains 1 bonus spice at Makers, accumulating; visiting gains all bonus spice. Deep Desert/Hagga additionally offer 4/2 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two/one worms. Wall protects Arrakeen, Refinery and Imperial Basin conflicts. Hooks are retained, not spent; a worm is placed directly in your Conflict, never garrison.
answers.evidence: Phase 4 Makers; Sandworms: Hooks requirement, Wall restriction, hooks never spent, worm directly to Conflict.

answers.answer: At end of a round, 10+ VP or empty Conflict deck triggers Endgame; first resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Tiebreaks: spice, Solari, water, garrison troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “At the end of a round”; Endgame Intrigue then most VP; listed tiebreakers.

answers.answer: CHOAM starts 2 contracts face up and 18 face down (from 20). Add 4 Imperium and 4 Intrigue cards. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; Components identify 10 contrasting-back contracts as Rise of Ix only.

answers.answer: Contract icon: take one face-up contract and replace it from bank face up; if none remain, get 2 Solari. Harvest requires visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown spice total that turn; Immediate completes when taken; Acquire TSFM on next acquisition.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts paragraphs.

answers.answer: No: if you take a contract for a space where your Agent was already sent this turn, wait for a future turn. On completion announce it, gain shown rewards, flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: “must wait until a future turn”; completion announce, rewards, flip and leave in supply.

answers.answer: One shared scoring Rival is third competitor. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective; humans randomly get the other two eligible Objectives, and the marked human gets First Player. Order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates only between humans. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival—Setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: Ignore occupied destination and reveal again. For two-destination cards use only the condition-matching one (Guild Influence or Conflict tier); if occupied, reveal again, not the other destination. Ignore normal costs/effects, applying Hagal effects only. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival—Agent turns and “Ignore normal space costs and effects.”

answers.answer: In 3–4 player setup, omit Objectives not marked for that player count, then each player draws one at random; the marked Objective holder takes First Player. Shaddam only with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched 1-3P/4/6P, each draws one, marked card takes First Player; Shaddam only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: Resources/sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if bank runs out. If personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: “not meant to be limited”; Recruiting; Setup payments returned to bank.

answers.answer: Round phases: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Reveal Conflict then resolve defensive bonus, then draw five. Recall checks endgame; otherwise recall Agents, pass First Player clockwise, start next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Player Reference.

answers.answer: Yes, space, Agent-box and Faction Influence effects may be done in any order. But requirements and costs must be paid before resolving any space or played-card effects, so visit Influence cannot meet entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay immediately before effects; “all these effects in any order.”

answers.answer: An arrow cost/effect can be paid/used only once per turn (except doubled Conflict rewards). Most effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrows, and black-X trash are optional. Intrigue conditions/costs must be met; direct self-trash instructions are mandatory.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy on an unoccupied observation post; some effects require a specific connected Agent icon. If no Spy remains in supply, you may first recall one for no effect.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: Infiltrate only lets you bypass another player’s occupancy, not your own Agent; it does not waive playing a matching card. You cannot use a Spy without playing a card for the Agent turn. You may recall two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, but not twice for Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies; FAQ Spies.

answers.answer: At Arrakeen, Refinery or Imperial Basin, visitor gets normal space effects; the controller separately gains respectively 1 Solari, 1 Solari or 1 spice, even if visitor is controller. Conflict winner takes control, replacing previous marker. Defensive troop comes from supply.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: Tie for second: each tied player gets third reward; winner retains own rewards/card and no further rewards. Tie for third gets nothing. Three-way tie for first: each gets second reward; no winner/card and nobody else gets rewards.
answers.evidence: Combat ties.

answers.answer: Three distinct positive strengths in three-player play: first and second receive normal rewards; third gets none. If Rival is one participant, ordinary 2–3-player rank and tie rules still apply.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 2 or 3 players first/second; third reward only for tie second; Rival counted in player count.

answers.answer: Plot during own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat only in Combat; Endgame at game end. Keep Intrigues face down separately, then after resolution put face up in discard next to deck. If deck empties, shuffle discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: Ordinary discard cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified; it means a chosen card from hand. Secrets steals one selected at random from each opponent with 4+ Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Steal Intrigue icon.

answers.answer: Trash can remove cards from hand, discard pile or in play; return ordinary cards to box, Reserve cards to Reserve stack. Optional unless cost or directed to trash itself. Trashing TSFM does not remove its acquired VP.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: Acquire box resolves once immediately when acquired. Reshuffle discard into deck when unable to draw because deck empty. Unused Persuasion is lost at end of Reveal and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Fremen Bond sees other Fremen cards played/revealed and still face up/in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order. They cease to be in play at Clean Up (unless trashed first).
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents, never the one just sent; it can be used again later that round. Retreat sends troop from Conflict to garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain-two Influence effect cannot split the two between Factions; both go to one chosen Faction. Alliance icon requires holding that Alliance; minimum-Influence effects require that minimum.
answers.evidence: Influence.

answers.answer: If holder loses Influence after being tied, one formerly tied player receives Alliance; if several, former holder chooses. Holder falling to 3 or lower loses Alliance; if no one has 4+, return token to board. VP follows token.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss.

answers.answer: Cards drawn during Reveal are immediately revealed and usable this turn; cards drawn after Reveal are held for next round, then five more are drawn. Plot with later Reveal effect stays face up until used, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: No: a “when you win” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If gained as reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If VP and all listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: You cannot delay: fulfill all contracts held for same space with one Agent placement. They resolve as Agent-turn effects in any order with space/card effects, but you must hold them when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with set-aside Sardaukar contracts; when taking a contract, Sardaukar Commander allows choosing one instead of generally available contract. Signet Ring restriction lasts only that Agent turn.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd token starts leftmost on Training track and stays at rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica starts Lady Jessica side up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: Moving 1→3 counts as reaching 2; can reach 2 again later after losing and regaining, only while moving up (not descending). Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor to discard does not trigger discard ability.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications.

answers.answer: Accept Contract (Spice Trade): draw a card, take a contract with CHOAM or 2 Solari without it; no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service (Emperor): gain 1 Emperor Influence and take contract/2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract and Dutiful Service; clarification that only actual Faction spaces award listed Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City, free, recruit 1 and draw 1, Combat. Fremkit: Fremen, free, +1 Influence and draw 1, Combat. Research Station: City, 2 water, recruit 2 and draw 2, Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water; gain accumulated bonus spice; choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, 2 worms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water; gain bonus; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, 1 worm. Choosing worms still grants all bonus spice. Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Deep Desert/Hagga Basin; Hooks not spent rule.

answers.answer: Requires 2+ Fremen Influence. Option 1: if lacking, take Hooks; recruit 1 and gain 1 water. Option 2: gain 1 water and optionally destroy Shield Wall. Wall-removal option does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: Each visit costs 5 Solari. First visit puts Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants +2 Persuasion every Reveal for rest of game. Later visits grant 2 spice, draw Intrigue, recruit 3. Not Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council.

answers.answer: Costs 8 Solari until anyone gets Swordmaster, then 6. Each player once per game; gain third Agent, usable this round and thereafter. Rival obtaining its Swordmaster lowers human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Landsraad icon; requires 2+ Emperor Influence; costs 3 Solari. May discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. No automatic Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege; clarification no automatic Influence except listed.

answers.answer: Spice Trade icon; requires 2+ Guild Influence; costs 3 spice; gain 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction, not necessarily Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support (Landsraad): choose 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2, and if pay also gain 1 water; not Combat. Spice Refinery (City), Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner (Guild, Combat): 5 spice, +1 Guild Influence, recruit 5. Desert Tactics (Fremen, Combat): 1 water, +1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1, optionally trash a card. Sardaukar (Emperor, not Combat): 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, draw Intrigue, recruit 4.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall (Landsraad): free, draw Intrigue; if Agent is there, +1 Persuasion during Reveal. Espionage (Bene Gesserit): 1 spice, +1 BG Influence, draw card, place Spy. Deliver Supplies (Guild): free, +1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; playable even if no opposing Spy is connected there. Ignore Litany Against Fear red box during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played as Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire removed card. You may acquire by other means without 1-Persuasion discount. If not acquired by end of your next Reveal, remove from game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate.

answers.answer: Rival starts 4 Influence cubes at track bottoms, 3 troops in garrison with rest in supply, 2 Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside board, 3 Spies, 1 water; score/combat marker 0. Keep 2P Reshuffle in Hagal deck. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival—Setup; Rival opening paragraph.

answers.answer: As soon as total Solari, spice, Intrigues and water reaches printed Swordmaster value, spend that amount. Count each item as one; spend Solari, then spice, Intrigues, water; keep leftovers. Agent is available this round immediately.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend any complete set of 7 Solari, or 7 spice, or 3 Intrigues, or 3 water for 1 VP each. Mixed total of seven does not qualify.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: exact sets listed.

answers.answer: Choose least-Influence Faction; ties use leftmost priority icon. Rival gains/loses VP and Alliances like human but not 4-Influence resource track bonus. Numbered Hagal Influence icon means position in Rival Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Influence effects; Rival resources paragraph.

answers.answer: No. For two-destination card choose only the destination matching condition (Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping; Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner). If occupied, reveal another Hagal card.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns.

answers.answer: Yes, at any Combat space deploy up to 2 available garrison troops even if card recruited none. At a noncombat space recruited units go to garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent placement; simply omit bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: at Combat deploy up to two even if none recruited; bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unrestricted Spy goes to first available Faction post in priority order; if all four occupied, ignore. Third and final supply Spy placement recalls the other two and triggers Scheme. Rival never Infiltrates or Gathers Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If Scheme recruits before Agent placement and same-turn visit is Combat, deploy those recruits too. A Place Spy card never places an Agent: attempt specified empty post, ignore if none, then reveal another Hagal card and continue turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards.

answers.answer: At Hagga/Deep Desert, always take all bonus spice. With Hooks and an unprotected Conflict, summon 1/2 worms instead of base spice; without Hooks or if Conflict is protected, take base 2/4 spice. Accumulated bonus spice is still collected.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces.

answers.answer: At beginning of Combat, if Rival has a unit deployed, reveal Hagal card and add bottom swords; if Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have normal Combat Intrigue window. No deployed unit means no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: Yes: Rival gets normal placement rewards, control, defensive supply troop, battle-icon VP and worm reward doubling. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay/recall required Spy. Contract reward gives 2 Solari; it never takes contracts.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: During Reveal effects, total/announce/set strength at any point and update as needed. Over 20, flip Combat marker to +20 side and start again from beginning of track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength.

answers.answer: Leader Signet Ring ability activates when Signet Ring is played on Agent turn, not when revealed. Cards can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader ability; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from post to supply, generally as cost for card effect. This is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recall-without-card options.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies; FAQ Spies.

answers.answer: “Trash an Intrigue” icon lets you choose one Intrigue from your hand to trash. Ordinary discard refers to a chosen card in hand and excludes Intrigue unless specified.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: Yes: sandworm-doubled reward granting 1 Influence of choice twice may go to same or two different Factions. A single effect granting two Influence with free choice cannot split; both go to one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice rule.

answers.answer: Resolve Rival’s printed Signet Ring ability from its selected Rival card; no human Signet Ring card or Reveal turn is needed. Rival follows printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities.
answers.evidence: Required Rival opening/setup: “follow its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities”; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Maker Hooks icon takes a Hook if it lacks one; if it already has one, no extra. Shield Wall removal occurs only if Rival has Hooks; otherwise ignored. If Wall already removed, removal has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces says Hook icon takes token “if needed”; wall removed only if Rival has Hooks. Whether repeated removal after wall gone has an effect is implicit, not stated.

answers.answer: Secrets: Bene Gesserit icon, no cost, not Combat. Gain 1 BG Influence and draw an Intrigue; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives you one chosen at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin: Spice Trade icon, no cost, Combat. Visitor gets 1 base plus all accumulated bonus spice. Controller gets 1 spice on each visit, even if same player.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin; controller clarification.

answers.answer: Place new Conflict face up next to deck on top of remaining prior Conflict cards; any unclaimed old card remains there underneath. Reveal it before each player draws five.
answers.evidence: Round Start.

answers.answer: Each human puts one cube at bottom of each of four Faction tracks; four Alliance tokens start on marked areas of those tracks, so nobody starts holding one. Shield Wall token begins in marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6.

answers.answer: First Player begins, then clockwise; after a player Reveals, skip that player for rest of phase. In 3–4 player play Player Turns ends when all have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, priority starts First Player and moves clockwise; eligible unit-holding players may play any number or pass, and window ends after consecutive passes from all involved players.
answers.evidence: Player Turns; Phase 3 Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Reveal remaining hand face up; resolve just-revealed cards’ Reveal effects; Clean Up all Agent and revealed cards to discard. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn three steps.

answers.answer: Shuffle each 10-card starting deck and place face down; shuffle Intrigue deck face down; shuffle Imperium deck face down and deal 5 face up as Row; Reserve in Prepare the Way and TSFM stacks. Combat marker starts 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6.

answers.answer: Ordinarily acquire any of five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card (Prepare the Way or TSFM). Cost appears top right. Ordinary purchases happen during Reveal using Persuasion.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes, human may decline Spy placement or Recall Spy even when legal. Shield Wall destruction icon is optional; if removed, it returns to box and cannot return later.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: ordinary placement/Recall Spy icons optional; Shield Wall token returned to box.

answers.answer: Played card must have Agent icon matching destination, unless Spy Agent icon and your connected Spy provide access. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card send there. If card has Spy Agent icon, it may send Agent to connected space.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Spy Agent icon rule.

answers.answer: Yes: play Plot during your Agent turn before placement and use its lawful resource gain to pay entry. No: resource from played Agent card or destination comes after placement and cannot pay that same entry.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before entry; later card/destination gains cannot pay same entry.

answers.answer: No. Skip Revealed humans but continue Rival Agent turns while it has Agents; begin Combat only once both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Player Turns two-player rules.

answers.answer: All 22 standard spaces (icon; Combat?): Accept Contract—Spice Trade, No; Arrakeen—City, Yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, No; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, Yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, No; Desert Tactics—Fremen, Yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, No; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, No; Fremkit—Fremen, Yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, No; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, Yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, Yes; High Council—Landsraad, No; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, Yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, No; Research Station—City, Yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, No; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, No; Shipping—Spice Trade, No; Sietch Tabr—City, Yes; Spice Refinery—City, Yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, No. Spy icon is an alternative only where card/post connection permits.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists each icon; “Combat” marked beside Arrakeen, Deep Desert, Desert Tactics, Fremkit, Hagga Basin, Heighliner, Imperial Basin, Research Station, Sietch Tabr, Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: At Round Start when Conflict is revealed, controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to that Conflict; optional and no Agent visit required. After all Combat rewards, return troops from Conflict to supply, reset all Combat markers to 0, and return worms to bank.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive troop; Combat cleanup.
